messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from today — thanks for the clarity on the new packaging. A few nitty-gritty questions I missed in the Q&A: how do credits interact with per-route rate limits for heavy embedding jobs?
sara (ceo): Short answer: credits are the billing unit; rate limits are throttles. You can exhaust credits but still be rate limited separately. We want predictable spend + predictable latency.
will (product): To add: for high-volume embedding pipelines we recommend a separate reserved bucket + a per-route quota that’s higher for embeddings. That avoids noisy-neighbor throttling.
megan (finance): Note: we do not auto-draw from reserved buckets unless customer enables it. Defaults are sandbox (dev) credits then main credits.
jon (eng): Practical detail — if you set a per-route quota, it applies before any credit deduction. So requests exceeding the quota are 429'd regardless of balance.
alex: If a customer has both Dedicated reserved capacity and hosted credits, which is billed first? and will there be grace overages?
sara (ceo): Dedicated commitments are invoiced as a commitment fee, not per-token credits. For hosted credits, they are consumed first for ad-hoc usage. We are working on a clear flow diagram in the billing docs.
kyle (solutions): For enterprise customers, we offer a configurable grace window (time-limited) for critical routes — agreed in the contract. Not automatic.
emily (support): Two common support asks: 1) dev teams accidentally burn credits in staging; 2) tests triggering rate caps. We usually suggest separate orgs/projects for staging plus a smaller dev bucket.
alex: Any plan to expose a live ‘credits burn by route’ feed in Console? would help ops.
will (product): Yes — roadmap item. We plan an initial rollout: token heatmap (by route/model) -> per-route burn + alerting (Q3).
megan (finance): Also adding a safety: email alerts at 70/90/100% of credit bucket, plus optional auto-topup (manual by default).
jon (eng): Technical note on fairshare: rate limiting uses a leaky-bucket + fairshare across API keys in the same org; we’re adding a ‘priority’ label so infra tests can be deprioritized.
alex: Is there a documented exemption process for CI/integration tests that need burst allowances?
kyle (solutions): Yes — open a support ticket with usage pattern and desired burst window. We review and, if approved, create a scoped exemption or temporary quota increase.
megan (finance): Exemptions are timeboxed and may require a payment method on file for post-burst billing.
infra-bot: deploy:rate-limits-service v2.4 rolled out to prod at 2024-11-06T18:02:12Z — added per-route metrics and quota API endpoints.
jon (eng): Example quota config we exposed in the Console API:
```json
{"route":"/v1/embeddings","org_quota":5000000,"route_quota":2000000,"burst":10000}
```
alex: Nice. One last: how will refunds / credits be handled if we auto-failover to a lower-cost model during outage?
sara (ceo): Policy — if we route to a fallback model that reduces cost/latency impact, we won’t retroactively refund credits; for material incidents that affect SLA, we handle on a case-by-case basis via support/SLA credits.
emily (support): If you think an incident warrants a review, submit an incident appeal with request id + time window and we’ll escalate.
alex: Thanks all. This helped— would love the flow diagram and the per-route burn plan when available. :thumbsup:
